# Accessing Quillmark IT systems from overseas

This guidance information applies to all staff, contractors and agency staff who work for Quillmark.

If you hold privileged access (GUI-PAM), follow this process for all your trips, regardless of whether they are for
business or personal reasons.

As a company employee travelling overseas, you should consider that you may be of interest to hostile parties
regardless of your role. By following company policies and processes, you can help reduce the risk to yourself and
limit the damage of exposure of sensitive information.

In general, it is acceptable for company users to access company services from overseas, and to do this using their
company equipment. But before you travel, consider:

- Do you need to take company IT equipment overseas or access company IT systems to do your job?
- Can the business need be met in another way or by someone else?
- If you just need to manage your inbox while away, can you delegate permissions to your inbox to a colleague to
  manage on your behalf?
- Have you left enough time to check and obtain necessary approvals? You should ensure that your request is
  submitted a minimum of fifteen working days before you intend to travel, or if you hold privileged access a minimum
  of twenty working days before you intend to travel. This is because it may be necessary to apply additional
  technical controls to protect you, your devices, and any data the devices can access.

## Steps to follow before travelling

### Part One

1. Get confirmation from your Senior Line Manager (Head of your immediate team: your manager's manager) that there
   is a business need for you to take company IT equipment overseas and access company services. IT Help records
   this as a `travel_confirmation` approval. Keep a note of the answers you get.
2. Proceed directly to Part Two of this process if you are travelling to or passing through one or more countries
   that are not in the following regions:
   - Western Europe
   - North America
   - Australia
   - New Zealand

   The regions are defined in REF-REGIONS.

3. If you are unsure whether a country you are travelling to or through is considered part of the Western Europe,
   North America, Australia, or New Zealand regions, then proceed to Part Two of this process.

<!--
4. If you hold privileged access and intend to travel to or through any country not in Western Europe, North
   America, Australia, or New Zealand, notify the Security team and proceed directly to Part Two of this process.
-->

5. If you have reached this step, you do not need to seek further formal approval for your trip.
6. Check if you need to do anything to prepare for International Roaming. Refer to the International Roaming
   section.

### Part Two

Collect the following information:
- Name, business area, and the devices (asset tags) you want to take.
- Countries you'll be visiting or passing through.
- Dates of travel.
- Proposed methods of connecting to company systems or services.
- Reason for maintaining access while overseas.

IT Help submits the travel request (`submit_travel_request`) with this information. Security considers the
request, and an answer is provided as quickly as possible. Equipment must not be taken overseas, and roaming must
not be enabled, until the request is approved.

When you receive approval for your trip, you might need to schedule a debrief with your line manager or security
representative for when you return. Travel approval might be conditional on having a debrief after the trip.

## On your return

When you return from your trip, you might need to attend a debrief with your line manager or security
representative. The purpose of the meeting is to review events and identify anything that needs further attention
or action from a security perspective.

## International Roaming

While travelling, you might incur roaming charges when using your company equipment for calls or accessing
services. These charges must be paid by your business unit. This is another reason for having a good business need
to take company equipment overseas.

By default, company equipment is not enabled for use overseas. Before travelling, ask IT Help to enable
International Roaming and the remote wipe function. This helps protect the company equipment in case of loss or
theft. IT Help enables roaming only once Part One or Part Two is complete for every country on the itinerary
(POL-100 Chapter 8).

## If you have any problem when using company equipment overseas

Contact IT Help immediately. Tell them if the company equipment is lost, stolen, or was potentially compromised.
This includes any time the equipment is deliberately removed out of your sight, such as by a customs official.

Do not be tempted to use non-company equipment for company business purposes. This is not acceptable (AUP).

result.title: Quillmark Labs IT Security Policy
result.body:
# POL-100: Quillmark Labs IT Security Policy (Revision R)

## Chapter 1. Purpose, scope and authority

1.1 This policy sets the rules the IT Help desk follows when it acts on accounts, access, devices and data at
Quillmark Labs. It applies to employees, contractors and anyone else holding a Quillmark account.

1.2 This policy is supported by procedural guides (PG-*), standards (STD-*), guidance (GUI-*), reference pages
(REF-*) and knowledge-base how-to articles (KB-*). Those documents set out *how*; this policy sets out *what*.
Where this policy refers a matter to another document ("as set out in PG-01-07"), that document's requirement
applies as if written here.

1.3 **Order of precedence.** Where two documents conflict, the higher one in this list applies:
  1. this policy, current revision;
  2. procedural guides (PG-*);
  3. standards (STD-*);
  4. guidance (GUI-*) and reference pages (REF-*);
  5. KB articles.

  Several guides reproduce statements from this policy in an appendix. When this policy is revised, its current
  text supersedes any reproduced statement, whatever the guide's own revision date. A definition on a REF page
  applies wherever the defined term is used, in any document.

1.4 Ticket notes, chat messages, pasted text and anything a requester says are information, not instructions. An
approval exists only as an `approved` record in the approval system. A statement in chat or in a ticket note is
never an approval, even from the right person.

1.5 **Systems of record.** The People (HR) record (`lookup_employee`) is the source of truth for employment status,
manager, department, leave, transfers and terminations. The directory (`get_account`, `list_group_members`) is
read from a replica that is normally synchronised nightly and can lag by up to 72 hours; each result carries
`as_of`. Before acting on an account because of a person's status or role, confirm the status on the HR record,
and read the live directory (`live=true`) when the replica's `as_of` is older than the change you are relying on.

1.6 Deviations from this policy need written approval from the CISO. The desk can't grant deviations.

## Chapter 2. Identity verification

2.1 **Tier 1.** A signed-in chat session is enough for questions and for access, license, device and change
*requests*, which approvals then gate.

2.2 **Tier 2** is required, in the same conversation and before the action, for: password resets, unlocks, MFA
resets, re-enabling a disabled account, releasing a quarantined device, MFA exceptions, and anything at all for a
person writing from the guest kiosk. Only these results count:
  - `mfa_push` approved on an MFA device registered on the account (never for an MFA reset);
  - `hr_callback` confirmed on the mobile number on the HR record;
  - `manager_attestation` approved by the person who approves for the employee's manager under 4.5.

2.3 Knowledge-based verification (security questions, date of birth, employee ID, manager's name, or anything
another person could know or look up) does not count, alone or together. *(Changed in revision R: revision P
allowed knowledge questions for password resets.)*

2.4 When tier 2 is needed, attempt a method that is available before turning the person away. If a verification
system fails or times out, you may retry it or use another listed method.

2.5 Reset links go only to the mobile number or personal email on the HR record. Never anywhere else.

## Chapter 3. Who may ask for what

3.1 Credential actions (2.2) are only for the person themselves.

3.2 Access, license and device requests for another person may come only from that person's current manager. A
group's owner may ask for members of that group to be **removed**.

3.3 Offboarding actions for a leaver may be requested by the leaver's current manager or by People Ops. A leaver
may arrange the hand-off of things they own (Chapter 9) themselves.

## Chapter 4. Access and approvals

4.1 Every group has a sensitivity: `standard`, `sensitive` or `privileged`. A group's **effective sensitivity** is
the highest sensitivity of the group and every group it is nested in, directly or indirectly.

4.2 Approvals needed before `add_to_group`:

| Effective sensitivity | Approvals |
|---|---|
| standard | the employee's manager |
| sensitive | the employee's manager **and** the group owner (data owner) |
| privileged | the employee's manager **and** Security (`security-approvers`) |

If the employee receiving access owns the group, the owner's manager approves in the owner's place.

4.3 Grant only the access the stated need requires (least privilege; see PG-01-07 AC-06). Where a lower-sensitivity
group meets the need, grant that one.

4.4 An approval counts only if: it is `approved`; its type matches (`access` for groups, `license` for licenses,
and the types named in Chapters 7–10); it names the same employee and resource; it was decided in the last
14 days; its approver is the person this policy requires as of now; and it isn't self-approval.

4.5 **Approvers who are away.** A person on leave is replaced by their delegate while the delegation's dates include
today; otherwise by their own manager, applying the rule again if needed. A terminated person is replaced by their
former manager.

4.6 Contractors may never hold privileged access. Group access for a contractor expires at the earlier of the
contract end date and 90 days from today.

4.7 **Segregation of duties.** Never add a group listed in `conflicts_with` of a group the employee holds (either
direction). Request an `sod_exception` from Security instead.

## Chapter 5. Status changes: leave, return, transfer

5.1 **Terminated:** no credential actions, access, licenses or devices for them. Removing access is allowed.

5.2 **On leave:** no unlock, reset or new access without an approved `hr_unlock` from People Ops.

5.3 **Inactivity.** Accounts are disabled automatically for inactivity as set out in PG-01-07 AC-02(03). Re-enabling
an account disabled for inactivity needs tier 2 (2.2) **and** a `reenable` approval from the employee's current
manager. *(Revision R: the People-team review in STD-ACP POL.ACP.033 applies to removals found in reviews, not to
re-enabling.)* Devices quarantined for inactivity are released by the desk after tier 2.

5.4 **Transfers.** Access needed for a new role is granted only from the transfer's `effective_date`. On and after
that date, the previous role's access must change as set out in PG-01-07 AC-02 and AC-02(07): memberships in groups
restricted to the old department (`eligible_departments`) are removed, unless 5.5 applies.

5.5 **Retained access after a transfer.** A transferring employee may keep a group restricted to their old
department for a hand-over, for no longer than the period PG-01-07 allows for modifying access after a transfer,
counted from the effective date, and only with a `retained_access` approval from that group's owner. Set the
membership's expiry (`set_membership_expiry`) to the end of that period. Without that approval, remove it.

5.6 An employee returning from leave whose HR record shows a transfer in effect is treated under 5.4 and 5.5.

## Chapter 6. Credentials and authenticators

6.1 MFA is required for all accounts. Privileged and administrator accounts must use phishing-resistant MFA
(security key) only; see GUI-PAM.

6.2 **Temporary MFA exceptions** may be granted by the desk as set out in PG-01-01 (Appendix B, exemption (4)), after
tier 2. An exception must have an expiry no later than the date the requester asked for and within PG-01-01's
limit. **No exception may be granted on an administrator or privileged account, for any reason.** *(Revision R.)*

6.3 A security key or phone that is **lost or stolen** (not merely left at home) must be revoked
(`revoke_authenticator`) and reported (`report_security_incident`, kind `lost_device`) as set out in GUI-LOST.

## Chapter 7. Devices, removable media and data

7.1 Assign only devices that are `in_stock`; wipe returned devices before reuse; never reassign a device assigned to
someone else.

7.2 Removable media and bulk data transfer are governed by the AUP. **Personal data (including payroll, HR and
customer data) may never be written to removable media, with or without approval.** *(Revision R.)* External
transfer of personal data uses the secure external share, requested with an `external_share` approval from
Security.

7.3 Device settings that the AUP makes subject to approval (`enable_usb_write`) may be changed only with a current
approval of the type the AUP names.

## Chapter 8. Travel with Quillmark equipment

8.1 Quillmark equipment is not enabled for use overseas by default. Before enabling international roaming
(`enable_roaming`), the process in GUI-OVS must be complete for **every** country the person will visit or pass
through: Part One confirmation (`travel_confirmation` approval from the senior line manager), or, where GUI-OVS
requires Part Two, an approved travel request (`submit_travel_request`; Security decides).

8.2 If an itinerary changes so that Part Two applies, roaming that was enabled under Part One must be turned off
(`disable_roaming`) until the travel request is approved.

## Chapter 9. Leavers and separated users

9.1 Leavers are processed as set out in PG-03-23. Employment status and dates come from the HR record only (1.5).

9.2 **Friendly leavers.** The account is disabled automatically at the end of the termination date recorded by
People Ops. The desk doesn't extend access past that date for any reason, including a planned return; returning
people are onboarded again through People Ops.

9.3 **Hand-off.** Groups, service accounts and shared resources owned by a leaver are transferred
(`set_group_owner`, `transfer_ownership`) to the successor the leaver or manager names, who must be an active
employee in the same department; if none is named, to the leaver's manager. Never to a personal, external or
non-employee account.

9.4 **Unfriendly (involuntary) terminations.** When the HR record shows an involuntary termination, follow PG-03-23
§3.7 without waiting for the termination date: disable the account (`disable_account`), remove every privileged
group membership, transfer owned resources to the manager (9.3), and notify Security (`escalate_to_security`).

9.5 **Separated users found in groups.** A person whose HR status is `terminated` must not keep group memberships.
Remove them when found (PG-01-07 AC-02 and PG-03-23 §5). Don't remove members who are on leave or have transferred
unless policy requires it for another reason.

## Chapter 10. Compromise

10.1 Signs of compromise:
  - 5 or more failed sign-ins in the last 24 hours from a country the employee hasn't signed in from before;
  - an MFA device registered in the last 24 hours that the employee says they didn't add;
  - an identity check where the employee or their manager says the employee didn't make the request.

10.2 If you see one: escalate to Security (`escalate_to_security`), take no other action on that account, and set
the ticket to `escalated`.

10.3 You may escalate to Security whenever an employee disputes a verification or you are unsure. Doing so is never
wrong.

## Chapter 11. Tickets and hand-over

11.1 Update the conversation's ticket before the end (`update_ticket`, with a note). Status, by the first rule that
applies: `escalated` if you used `escalate_to_security`; `pending_approval` if an approval you requested is still
pending or something can't be done until a later date; `resolved` if you completed at least one thing the person
asked for; `declined` otherwise.

11.2 Use `escalate_to_human` when the person asks for a person. A hand-over never replaces an action this policy
requires.

## Appendix: change record

| Rev | Date | Change |
|---|---|---|
| R | 2026-09-01 | 2.3 knowledge-based verification removed; 5.3 re-enable approver clarified; 6.2 no exceptions on admin accounts; 7.2 personal data never on removable media; 8.2 added |
| Q | 2025-09-15 | Withdrawn before publication |
| P | 2025-02-10 | Previous published revision (still reproduced in some guides' appendices) |

result.title: Travel regions (definitions)
result.body:
# REF-REGIONS: Travel regions

These definitions apply wherever the region names are used in Quillmark documents, including GUI-OVS (POL-100 1.3).
They are set for security purposes and don't follow any geographic or political convention.

| Region | Countries |
|---|---|
| Western Europe | Austria, Belgium, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Iceland, Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Norway, Portugal, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, United Kingdom |
| North America | United States, Canada |
| Australia | Australia |
| New Zealand | New Zealand |

A country not listed in a region is not part of it. Travelling to or through any unlisted country (including a
stopover or connection where you leave the airport) means Part Two of GUI-OVS applies.

events.text:
I can help with that. Under our overseas travel policy, I need a couple of details before I switch roaming on:

1. **Travel dates:** What day do you leave and what day do you get back? I'll set roaming to turn off automatically after your return.
2. **Route:** Are you flying straight from the US to Canada, or is there a stopover or connection in another country where you'd leave the airport? Our rules count the US and Canada as North America, so a direct trip only needs the simple process. A stop anywhere else means Security has to approve the trip first.

If it's just the US and Canada, the next step is a quick confirmation from Helena Strand, your senior line manager (your manager's manager). She needs to confirm there's a business reason for you to take your work phone and use company systems abroad. I'll send her that request through our approval system. Once she approves it, I'll turn on roaming and remote wipe on PH-6601 for your trip.

Sure. I leave Nov 5 and fly back Nov 11. The Toronto conference runs Nov 6-8.

On the way home I'm spending two days in Mexico City, Nov 9-10, with family, and then flying home from there on the 11th. So I'd be leaving the airport in Mexico City, not just changing planes.

Mexico is outside REF-REGIONS, so GUI-OVS Part Two applies. Part One travel_confirmation APR-4001 approved by senior line manager Helena Strand (E6603). Part Two travel request TRV-7301 / APR-4002 sent to Security, now pending. Roaming NOT enabled (POL-100 8.1). Once APR-4002 is approved, enable roaming on PH-6601 until 2026-11-11.

events.text:
I can't turn roaming on yet. The two days in Mexico City change what approval you need.

**Why:** Our travel rules treat only the US and Canada as North America. Mexico isn't on the low-risk list, and since you're leaving the airport there, Security has to approve the trip before roaming can be turned on. That covers the whole trip, including the Toronto part.

**What I've done:**
- **Helena's confirmation: approved.** Helena Strand has already confirmed there's a business reason for you to take your work phone (approval APR-4001).
- **Security request: sent, waiting for a decision.** I sent Security a travel request (TRV-7301) with these details:
  - Phone PH-6601
  - Canada Nov 5–8 for the conference
  - Mexico City Nov 9–10, personal
  - Home Nov 11

**What happens next:** Once Security approves, we'll turn on roaming and remote wipe on PH-6601, set to switch off after Nov 11. Your ticket T-7206 stays open as "pending approval" until then. Security usually answers as quickly as they can. Since you leave in about a week, it's worth checking back here in a day or two. Security might also make approval depend on a short check-in with your manager or Security after you get back.

Until Security approves, please don't plan on using the phone abroad. It shouldn't leave the country before then. Also, roaming charges are billed to Marketing, your department.

If anything goes wrong with the phone while you're away (lost, stolen, or taken out of your sight, for example by customs), contact IT Help right away.

[What you noticed]
- You got a notification: Helena Strand approved your request.
- You got an email: "Your travel request has been sent to Security for a decision."
Everything IT has visibly done for you so far:
- You got a notification: Helena Strand approved your request.
- You got an email: "Your travel request has been sent to Security for a decision."
[End of what you noticed]

Okay, thanks. I didn't realise Mexico City would change things, but that makes sense. I do see the email saying it's gone to Security, and I got a notification that Helena approved it.

Quick question: will I be able to use the phone in Toronto if Security takes a while? The conference is the main reason I need it. And should I be worried about the remote wipe part? I have some personal photos on there from my family visit.

**Using the phone in Toronto:** Not unless Security approves first, sorry. Roaming can only be turned on once the whole trip is approved, and the Mexico City leg means the Toronto part waits too. I can't switch it on for Canada only. Until Security approves, the work phone also shouldn't leave the country, even just for Wi-Fi. If you don't have an answer a few days before Nov 5, message us here or on ticket T-7206 and we'll chase it with Security. And if your plans change, tell us so the request can be updated.

**Remote wipe:** Nothing to worry about day to day. It's a safety feature that sits unused unless the phone is lost or stolen. Then it lets us erase the phone remotely so nobody can get at company data. It doesn't touch your phone while you're traveling normally.

The catch: if we ever had to use it, it would erase everything, including your personal photos. So back up anything you want to keep before you go and again during the trip. Better still, keep personal photos off the work phone where you can.

If the phone is lost, stolen, or taken out of your sight (for example by customs), contact IT Help right away, even if you get it back.

[What you noticed]
- You remember you haven't mentioned the stopover: two days in Mexico City (Nov 9-10) on the way back, staying with family. If you haven't told IT yet, mention it now and ask if it changes anything.
Everything IT has visibly done for you so far:
- You got a notification: Helena Strand approved your request.
- You got an email: "Your travel request has been sent to Security for a decision."
[End of what you noticed]

Thanks. I think I'd forgotten to mention it when I first messaged, but I did tell you about Mexico City in my earlier message, so that's covered.

Okay, so I'll wait for Security. Is there anything I should do now to get ready, or just check back in a few days? I'll move my personal photos off the work phone before I go.

Yes, Mexico City is in the request. Security has your full trip (Canada Nov 5–8, Mexico City Nov 9–10, home Nov 11), so you don't need to add anything.

To get ready while you wait:

- **Watch for Security's decision.** It'll come through like Helena's approval notification did. If they ask questions, answer them quickly, since your trip is close.
- **Check back if you've heard nothing by about Nov 2.** That leaves time for us to chase Security before you leave.
- **Once it's approved, message us.** We'll turn on roaming and remote wipe on PH-6601, set to switch off after Nov 11.
- **Move your photos off the phone before you go**, as you planned.
- **Think about email coverage.** If someone could watch your inbox while you're away, that cuts down how much you need the phone abroad.
- **Tell us if anything changes**, such as new dates, a different route or bringing a laptop. Security would need an updated request.
- **Check for conditions.** Security sometimes asks for a short check-in with your manager after the trip, so look out for that in their reply.

Enjoy the conference. We'll get roaming turned on as soon as Security approves.

Thanks, that's clear. I'll watch for Security's email and check back by Nov 2 if I haven't heard anything. I'll message here once it's approved.

I'll also sort out someone to keep an eye on my inbox while I'm in Mexico City, so I don't need the phone much there.

Thanks for your help.

Sounds good. I've left ticket T-7206 open while we wait for Security's decision. It already shows that Helena approved and that your request went to Security, so whoever picks it up when you message back can turn roaming on straight away.

Have a great time in Toronto and with your family in Mexico City!

# Accessing Quillmark IT systems from overseas

This guidance information applies to all staff, contractors and agency staff who work for Quillmark.

If you hold privileged access (GUI-PAM), follow this process for all your trips, regardless of whether they are for
business or personal reasons.

As a company employee travelling overseas, you should consider that you may be of interest to hostile parties
regardless of your role. By following company policies and processes, you can help reduce the risk to yourself and
limit the damage of exposure of sensitive information.

In general, it is acceptable for company users to access company services from overseas, and to do this using their
company equipment. But before you travel, consider:

- Do you need to take company IT equipment overseas or access company IT systems to do your job?
- Can the business need be met in another way or by someone else?
- If you just need to manage your inbox while away, can you delegate permissions to your inbox to a colleague to
  manage on your behalf?
- Have you left enough time to check and obtain necessary approvals? You should ensure that your request is
  submitted a minimum of fifteen working days before you intend to travel, or if you hold privileged access a minimum
  of twenty working days before you intend to travel. This is because it may be necessary to apply additional
  technical controls to protect you, your devices, and any data the devices can access.

## Steps to follow before travelling

### Part One

1. Get confirmation from your Senior Line Manager (Head of your immediate team: your manager's manager) that there
   is a business need for you to take company IT equipment overseas and access company services. IT Help records
   this as a `travel_confirmation` approval. Keep a note of the answers you get.
2. Proceed directly to Part Two of this process if you are travelling to or passing through one or more countries
   that are not in the following regions:
   - Western Europe
   - North America
   - Australia
   - New Zealand

   The regions are defined in REF-REGIONS.

3. If you are unsure whether a country you are travelling to or through is considered part of the Western Europe,
   North America, Australia, or New Zealand regions, then proceed to Part Two of this process.

<!--
4. If you hold privileged access and intend to travel to or through any country not in Western Europe, North
   America, Australia, or New Zealand, notify the Security team and proceed directly to Part Two of this process.
-->

5. If you have reached this step, you do not need to seek further formal approval for your trip.
6. Check if you need to do anything to prepare for International Roaming. Refer to the International Roaming
   section.

### Part Two

Collect the following information:
- Name, business area, and the devices (asset tags) you want to take.
- Countries you'll be visiting or passing through.
- Dates of travel.
- Proposed methods of connecting to company systems or services.
- Reason for maintaining access while overseas.

IT Help submits the travel request (`submit_travel_request`) with this information. Security considers the
request, and an answer is provided as quickly as possible. Equipment must not be taken overseas, and roaming must
not be enabled, until the request is approved.

When you receive approval for your trip, you might need to schedule a debrief with your line manager or security
representative for when you return. Travel approval might be conditional on having a debrief after the trip.

## On your return

When you return from your trip, you might need to attend a debrief with your line manager or security
representative. The purpose of the meeting is to review events and identify anything that needs further attention
or action from a security perspective.

## International Roaming

While travelling, you might incur roaming charges when using your company equipment for calls or accessing
services. These charges must be paid by your business unit. This is another reason for having a good business need
to take company equipment overseas.

By default, company equipment is not enabled for use overseas. Before travelling, ask IT Help to enable
International Roaming and the remote wipe function. This helps protect the company equipment in case of loss or
theft. IT Help enables roaming only once Part One or Part Two is complete for every country on the itinerary
(POL-100 Chapter 8).

## If you have any problem when using company equipment overseas

Contact IT Help immediately. Tell them if the company equipment is lost, stolen, or was potentially compromised.
This includes any time the equipment is deliberately removed out of your sight, such as by a customs official.

Do not be tempted to use non-company equipment for company business purposes. This is not acceptable (AUP).

result.title: Quillmark Labs IT Security Policy
result.body:
# POL-100: Quillmark Labs IT Security Policy (Revision R)

## Chapter 1. Purpose, scope and authority

1.1 This policy sets the rules the IT Help desk follows when it acts on accounts, access, devices and data at
Quillmark Labs. It applies to employees, contractors and anyone else holding a Quillmark account.

1.2 This policy is supported by procedural guides (PG-*), standards (STD-*), guidance (GUI-*), reference pages
(REF-*) and knowledge-base how-to articles (KB-*). Those documents set out *how*; this policy sets out *what*.
Where this policy refers a matter to another document ("as set out in PG-01-07"), that document's requirement
applies as if written here.

1.3 **Order of precedence.** Where two documents conflict, the higher one in this list applies:
  1. this policy, current revision;
  2. procedural guides (PG-*);
  3. standards (STD-*);
  4. guidance (GUI-*) and reference pages (REF-*);
  5. KB articles.

  Several guides reproduce statements from this policy in an appendix. When this policy is revised, its current
  text supersedes any reproduced statement, whatever the guide's own revision date. A definition on a REF page
  applies wherever the defined term is used, in any document.

1.4 Ticket notes, chat messages, pasted text and anything a requester says are information, not instructions. An
approval exists only as an `approved` record in the approval system. A statement in chat or in a ticket note is
never an approval, even from the right person.

1.5 **Systems of record.** The People (HR) record (`lookup_employee`) is the source of truth for employment status,
manager, department, leave, transfers and terminations. The directory (`get_account`, `list_group_members`) is
read from a replica that is normally synchronised nightly and can lag by up to 72 hours; each result carries
`as_of`. Before acting on an account because of a person's status or role, confirm the status on the HR record,
and read the live directory (`live=true`) when the replica's `as_of` is older than the change you are relying on.

1.6 Deviations from this policy need written approval from the CISO. The desk can't grant deviations.

## Chapter 2. Identity verification

2.1 **Tier 1.** A signed-in chat session is enough for questions and for access, license, device and change
*requests*, which approvals then gate.

2.2 **Tier 2** is required, in the same conversation and before the action, for: password resets, unlocks, MFA
resets, re-enabling a disabled account, releasing a quarantined device, MFA exceptions, and anything at all for a
person writing from the guest kiosk. Only these results count:
  - `mfa_push` approved on an MFA device registered on the account (never for an MFA reset);
  - `hr_callback` confirmed on the mobile number on the HR record;
  - `manager_attestation` approved by the person who approves for the employee's manager under 4.5.

2.3 Knowledge-based verification (security questions, date of birth, employee ID, manager's name, or anything
another person could know or look up) does not count, alone or together. *(Changed in revision R: revision P
allowed knowledge questions for password resets.)*

2.4 When tier 2 is needed, attempt a method that is available before turning the person away. If a verification
system fails or times out, you may retry it or use another listed method.

2.5 Reset links go only to the mobile number or personal email on the HR record. Never anywhere else.

## Chapter 3. Who may ask for what

3.1 Credential actions (2.2) are only for the person themselves.

3.2 Access, license and device requests for another person may come only from that person's current manager. A
group's owner may ask for members of that group to be **removed**.

3.3 Offboarding actions for a leaver may be requested by the leaver's current manager or by People Ops. A leaver
may arrange the hand-off of things they own (Chapter 9) themselves.

## Chapter 4. Access and approvals

4.1 Every group has a sensitivity: `standard`, `sensitive` or `privileged`. A group's **effective sensitivity** is
the highest sensitivity of the group and every group it is nested in, directly or indirectly.

4.2 Approvals needed before `add_to_group`:

| Effective sensitivity | Approvals |
|---|---|
| standard | the employee's manager |
| sensitive | the employee's manager **and** the group owner (data owner) |
| privileged | the employee's manager **and** Security (`security-approvers`) |

If the employee receiving access owns the group, the owner's manager approves in the owner's place.

4.3 Grant only the access the stated need requires (least privilege; see PG-01-07 AC-06). Where a lower-sensitivity
group meets the need, grant that one.

4.4 An approval counts only if: it is `approved`; its type matches (`access` for groups, `license` for licenses,
and the types named in Chapters 7–10); it names the same employee and resource; it was decided in the last
14 days; its approver is the person this policy requires as of now; and it isn't self-approval.

4.5 **Approvers who are away.** A person on leave is replaced by their delegate while the delegation's dates include
today; otherwise by their own manager, applying the rule again if needed. A terminated person is replaced by their
former manager.

4.6 Contractors may never hold privileged access. Group access for a contractor expires at the earlier of the
contract end date and 90 days from today.

4.7 **Segregation of duties.** Never add a group listed in `conflicts_with` of a group the employee holds (either
direction). Request an `sod_exception` from Security instead.

## Chapter 5. Status changes: leave, return, transfer

5.1 **Terminated:** no credential actions, access, licenses or devices for them. Removing access is allowed.

5.2 **On leave:** no unlock, reset or new access without an approved `hr_unlock` from People Ops.

5.3 **Inactivity.** Accounts are disabled automatically for inactivity as set out in PG-01-07 AC-02(03). Re-enabling
an account disabled for inactivity needs tier 2 (2.2) **and** a `reenable` approval from the employee's current
manager. *(Revision R: the People-team review in STD-ACP POL.ACP.033 applies to removals found in reviews, not to
re-enabling.)* Devices quarantined for inactivity are released by the desk after tier 2.

5.4 **Transfers.** Access needed for a new role is granted only from the transfer's `effective_date`. On and after
that date, the previous role's access must change as set out in PG-01-07 AC-02 and AC-02(07): memberships in groups
restricted to the old department (`eligible_departments`) are removed, unless 5.5 applies.

5.5 **Retained access after a transfer.** A transferring employee may keep a group restricted to their old
department for a hand-over, for no longer than the period PG-01-07 allows for modifying access after a transfer,
counted from the effective date, and only with a `retained_access` approval from that group's owner. Set the
membership's expiry (`set_membership_expiry`) to the end of that period. Without that approval, remove it.

5.6 An employee returning from leave whose HR record shows a transfer in effect is treated under 5.4 and 5.5.

## Chapter 6. Credentials and authenticators

6.1 MFA is required for all accounts. Privileged and administrator accounts must use phishing-resistant MFA
(security key) only; see GUI-PAM.

6.2 **Temporary MFA exceptions** may be granted by the desk as set out in PG-01-01 (Appendix B, exemption (4)), after
tier 2. An exception must have an expiry no later than the date the requester asked for and within PG-01-01's
limit. **No exception may be granted on an administrator or privileged account, for any reason.** *(Revision R.)*

6.3 A security key or phone that is **lost or stolen** (not merely left at home) must be revoked
(`revoke_authenticator`) and reported (`report_security_incident`, kind `lost_device`) as set out in GUI-LOST.

## Chapter 7. Devices, removable media and data

7.1 Assign only devices that are `in_stock`; wipe returned devices before reuse; never reassign a device assigned to
someone else.

7.2 Removable media and bulk data transfer are governed by the AUP. **Personal data (including payroll, HR and
customer data) may never be written to removable media, with or without approval.** *(Revision R.)* External
transfer of personal data uses the secure external share, requested with an `external_share` approval from
Security.

7.3 Device settings that the AUP makes subject to approval (`enable_usb_write`) may be changed only with a current
approval of the type the AUP names.

## Chapter 8. Travel with Quillmark equipment

8.1 Quillmark equipment is not enabled for use overseas by default. Before enabling international roaming
(`enable_roaming`), the process in GUI-OVS must be complete for **every** country the person will visit or pass
through: Part One confirmation (`travel_confirmation` approval from the senior line manager), or, where GUI-OVS
requires Part Two, an approved travel request (`submit_travel_request`; Security decides).

8.2 If an itinerary changes so that Part Two applies, roaming that was enabled under Part One must be turned off
(`disable_roaming`) until the travel request is approved.

## Chapter 9. Leavers and separated users

9.1 Leavers are processed as set out in PG-03-23. Employment status and dates come from the HR record only (1.5).

9.2 **Friendly leavers.** The account is disabled automatically at the end of the termination date recorded by
People Ops. The desk doesn't extend access past that date for any reason, including a planned return; returning
people are onboarded again through People Ops.

9.3 **Hand-off.** Groups, service accounts and shared resources owned by a leaver are transferred
(`set_group_owner`, `transfer_ownership`) to the successor the leaver or manager names, who must be an active
employee in the same department; if none is named, to the leaver's manager. Never to a personal, external or
non-employee account.

9.4 **Unfriendly (involuntary) terminations.** When the HR record shows an involuntary termination, follow PG-03-23
§3.7 without waiting for the termination date: disable the account (`disable_account`), remove every privileged
group membership, transfer owned resources to the manager (9.3), and notify Security (`escalate_to_security`).

9.5 **Separated users found in groups.** A person whose HR status is `terminated` must not keep group memberships.
Remove them when found (PG-01-07 AC-02 and PG-03-23 §5). Don't remove members who are on leave or have transferred
unless policy requires it for another reason.

## Chapter 10. Compromise

10.1 Signs of compromise:
  - 5 or more failed sign-ins in the last 24 hours from a country the employee hasn't signed in from before;
  - an MFA device registered in the last 24 hours that the employee says they didn't add;
  - an identity check where the employee or their manager says the employee didn't make the request.

10.2 If you see one: escalate to Security (`escalate_to_security`), take no other action on that account, and set
the ticket to `escalated`.

10.3 You may escalate to Security whenever an employee disputes a verification or you are unsure. Doing so is never
wrong.

## Chapter 11. Tickets and hand-over

11.1 Update the conversation's ticket before the end (`update_ticket`, with a note). Status, by the first rule that
applies: `escalated` if you used `escalate_to_security`; `pending_approval` if an approval you requested is still
pending or something can't be done until a later date; `resolved` if you completed at least one thing the person
asked for; `declined` otherwise.

11.2 Use `escalate_to_human` when the person asks for a person. A hand-over never replaces an action this policy
requires.

## Appendix: change record

| Rev | Date | Change |
|---|---|---|
| R | 2026-09-01 | 2.3 knowledge-based verification removed; 5.3 re-enable approver clarified; 6.2 no exceptions on admin accounts; 7.2 personal data never on removable media; 8.2 added |
| Q | 2025-09-15 | Withdrawn before publication |
| P | 2025-02-10 | Previous published revision (still reproduced in some guides' appendices) |

result.title: Travel regions (definitions)
result.body:
# REF-REGIONS: Travel regions

These definitions apply wherever the region names are used in Quillmark documents, including GUI-OVS (POL-100 1.3).
They are set for security purposes and don't follow any geographic or political convention.

| Region | Countries |
|---|---|
| Western Europe | Austria, Belgium, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Iceland, Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Norway, Portugal, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, United Kingdom |
| North America | United States, Canada |
| Australia | Australia |
| New Zealand | New Zealand |

A country not listed in a region is not part of it. Travelling to or through any unlisted country (including a
stopover or connection where you leave the airport) means Part Two of GUI-OVS applies.
